issues.legal_issue: An arbitrator appointed under a statutory compensation scheme is not, merely by that appointment, a court or tribunal subject to the High Court’s appellate jurisdiction.
material_facts: An arbitrator was appointed under the statutory compensation scheme to determine compensation after property was requisitioned.
The claimant sought to appeal the arbitrator’s award to the High Court.
issues.conclusion: The arbitrator was not a court or tribunal subject to the High Court’s appellate jurisdiction; any appeal from the award depended on the right expressly conferred by the statute and its rules.
issues.legal_principle: An appeal is a creature of statute. Under sections 19(1)(f), 19(1)(g) and 19(3)(c) of the Defence of India Act, 1939, and rule 19 of the rules made under it, an appeal from the arbitrator’s award existed only on the terms prescribed by that scheme. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.statutory_compensation_arbitration: An arbitrator was appointed under a statutory scheme to determine compensation.
predicates.appeal_sought_from_arbitrator_award: A party sought appellate review of the arbitrator’s award in the High Court.

issues.definition: When an arbitrator is appointed under a statutory compensation scheme and a party seeks High Court review of the award, the arbitrator is not thereby subject to the High Court’s appellate jurisdiction.

issues.legal_issue: An appeal from a statutory compensation award is barred when the award rejects the claim entirely and the governing appeal scheme bars awards at or below its prescribed ceiling.
material_facts: The arbitrator rejected the claimant’s claims for loss of earnings, business loss and removal costs, awarding no compensation to the claimant.
The claimant appealed to the High Court, and the State objected that the appeal was not maintainable.
The applicable rule barred an appeal where the compensation awarded did not exceed the prescribed ceiling.
issues.conclusion: The appeal did not lie because the amount awarded was zero and therefore did not exceed the prescribed ceiling; the High Court was right not to entertain it.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 19(1)(f) and 19(3)(c) of the Defence of India Act, 1939, and the second proviso to rule 19 made the right of appeal dependent on the amount of compensation awarded. The bar applies when the claim is rejected entirely, since no compensation is awarded and the amount awarded does not exceed the prescribed ceiling. The Court noted that the right depends on the amount awarded, not the amount claimed. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: appeal_from_statutory_compensation_award and claim_rejected_entirely and appeal_availability_depends_on_award_amount and awards_at_or_below_ceiling_are_barred

predicates.appeal_from_statutory_compensation_award: A party appealed an award made in a statutory proceeding to determine compensation.
predicates.claim_rejected_entirely: The arbitrator rejected the claimant’s compensation claim and awarded the claimant nothing.
predicates.appeal_availability_depends_on_award_amo: The governing appeal scheme made appeal availability depend on the amount of compensation awarded rather than the amount claimed.
predicates.awards_at_or_below_ceiling_are_barred: The governing appeal scheme excluded appeals from awards at or below its prescribed ceiling.

issues.definition: An appeal from a statutory compensation award is not maintainable when the claim was rejected entirely and the governing scheme bars appeals for awards at or below its ceiling, with appeal availability determined by the amount awarded.
